narration.en: Vanadium in solution can be violet, green, blue or yellow, one colour for each oxidation state from +2 to +5. Variable oxidation states are a hallmark of transition metals.

body.en: Because the ns and (n−1)d energies are close, transition metals can lose different numbers of electrons, giving oxidation states that usually differ by one (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Cu⁺/Cu²⁺). The number of states is greatest near the middle of the series: Mn shows +2 to +7. Sc shows only +3 and Zn only +2. The highest states appear in oxides and fluorides: oxygen stabilises them better because it can form multiple bonds, so Mn reaches +7 in Mn₂O₇ but only +4 in MnF₄. Low states (0) appear in carbonyls such as Ni(CO)₄.
body.kn: ns ಮತ್ತು (n−1)d ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳು ಹತ್ತಿರವಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣ ಲೋಹಗಳು ವಿವಿಧ ಆಕ್ಸಿಡೀಕರಣ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗಳನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯ ಮಧ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು: Mn +2 ರಿಂದ +7. ಅತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗಳು ಆಕ್ಸೈಡ್ ಮತ್ತು ಫ್ಲೋರೈಡ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ.

points.en: Maximum number near the middle (Mn: +2 to +7)
Oxygen stabilises higher states than fluorine (Mn₂O₇ vs MnF₄)

body.en: E°(M²⁺/M) depends on the enthalpy of atomisation, the ionisation enthalpies and the hydration enthalpy. Across the 3d series it becomes less negative; Cu (+0.34 V) is the only one that is positive. For M³⁺/M²⁺: Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ (+1.57 V) and Co³⁺/Co²⁺ (+1.97 V) are high, so Mn³⁺ and Co³⁺ are strong oxidising agents; Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ (−0.41 V) is negative, so Cr²⁺ is a strong reducing agent. The low E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) of +0.77 V reflects the extra stability of Fe³⁺ (d⁵).
body.kn: E°(M²⁺/M) ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಋಣವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ತಾಮ್ರದ್ದು ಮಾತ್ರ ಧನ. Mn³⁺ ಮತ್ತು Co³⁺ ಪ್ರಬಲ ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಕಗಳು; Cr²⁺ ಪ್ರಬಲ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಕ.

points.en: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V: Cu does not liberate H₂ from acids
Stable d³ (Cr³⁺), d⁵ (Mn²⁺, Fe³⁺) and d¹⁰ configurations drive these trends
